newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso at 30.50 to dollar in black market.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso at 30.50 to dollar in black market.

text.p: The peso settled at 30.50 to the U.S. dollar in the unofficial parallel market in Manila, weaker than the 29 peso close in the official market, traders said on Monday.

The black market rate fell to as low as 33 to 34 pesos on Friday when the Central Bank announced it was allowing the peso to trade within a wider range. The peso was trading between 26.50 and 26.75 on Thursday.
On Monday, the first deal in the black market was done at 28 pesos and it crept down steadily as uncertainty hung over the Philippine Dealing System, they said.
"The opening bid-and-offer quotes were very wide in the morning, ranging from 29 to 36 pesos. Of course, there were no done deals," a trader at a foreign exchange firm said.
Traders later adjusted the range to 28 and 31.
"The market was very cautious. Most stayed away from quoting," another trader said.
Before the de facto devaluation, black market rates were hovering 10 to 20 centavos lower than the official rates.
Foreign exchange firms deal with money changers and businessmen who do not have proper import documents to buy dollars from the banks.
The parallel market opens at 9:00 a.m. (0100 GMT) and closes at noon (0400 GMT) to allow settlements in the afternoon.
